title: Area, and how fast it grows

intro.say: Three things a graph can now do: grow an area, draw the area as a curve of its own, and show a jump.

beats.say: Start at zero and sweep the right edge across. The area under the curve adds up as it goes.
By the time the edge reaches 6, the total is {total.area}.

chapters.title: The area is a curve too
chapters.say: Record that total at every x.

beats.say: Record the running total at every x and you get a second curve, the area function, A of x.
Shade up to 2 and the area is {s.area}. The new curve is exactly that high there: {p.y}.
Now measure how fast the area is growing at 2. Its slope is {m.slope}.
And the height of the original curve at 2 is {h.y}. The same number.
Slide along, and the slope of the area keeps matching the height of the curve.

chapters.title: Jumps
chapters.say: And one more mark: an arrow from point to point.

scenes.heading: A step that is too big
scenes.name: f

beats.say: Walk downhill on this bowl in small steps, and each jump lands closer to the bottom.
Take steps that are too big, and each jump clears the bottom and lands higher on the other side.
